statement: (i) Solve $\ln x+\ln(x-2)=\ln 3$. (ii) Show that $\ln(1+x)<x$ for all $x>0$. (iii) Deduce that $\ln 2<1$ and $\ln(1+\frac1n)<\frac1n$ for $n\ge1$.
solution: (i) $\ln(x(x-2))=\ln 3\Rightarrow x^{2}-2x-3=0\Rightarrow x=3$ (the root $x=-1$ is invalid since $x>2$). (ii) Let $f(x)=x-\ln(1+x)$; $f(0)=0$ and $f'(x)=1-\frac1{1+x}=\frac{x}{1+x}>0$ for $x>0$, so $f(x)>0$, i.e. $\ln(1+x)<x$. (iii) With $x=1$: $\ln 2<1$. With $x=1/n$: $\ln(1+1/n)<1/n$.
